name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) - Girl Child Savings Account
benefit: Government-backed savings account for a girl child under the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao initiative. Interest rate 8.2% per annum compounded annually (current rate as of July-Sept 2026; reviewed quarterly by the government - the highest among small savings schemes). Deposits: minimum Rs 250 and maximum Rs 1.5 lakh per financial year, for 15 years from account opening; the account matures 21 years after opening. Fully tax-free (EEE): deposits qualify for Section 80C deduction, and interest plus maturity amount are income-tax free. Partial withdrawal up to 50% of balance allowed for the girl's higher education after she turns 18 (or passes class 10); premature closure permitted on her marriage after age 18. Account is transferable across any post office or authorized bank in India. Illustration: Rs 1.5 lakh/year for 15 years grows to roughly Rs 63-65 lakh at maturity at the current rate.
eligibility_rules: Account can be opened in the name of a girl child any time before she turns 10 years old
Only a parent or court-appointed legal guardian can open and operate the account (until the girl turns 18); grandparents cannot open it unless they are the legal guardian
The girl child must be a resident Indian at account opening
Only ONE account per girl child
Maximum two accounts per family (i.e. for two daughters); exception: twins/triplets allow a third account with birth certificates as proof
Account can be opened at any post office or authorized bank branch with a minimum deposit of Rs 250
exclusions: Girls aged 10 or above at the time of opening are not eligible
Boys are not eligible - the scheme is exclusively for girl children
A third account in a family is not allowed (except for twins/triplets)
NRI families cannot open the account; if the girl/family becomes non-resident after opening, interest stops accruing from that date and the account must be closed
Depositing more than Rs 1.5 lakh in a financial year earns no interest on the excess
If the minimum Rs 250 yearly deposit is missed, the account becomes 'defaulted' (revivable with a Rs 50 penalty per year)
documents_required: Birth certificate of the girl child
Identity proof of the parent/guardian (Aadhaar / PAN)
Account opening form (Form-1) at the post office or bank
how_to_apply: Visit any post office or authorized bank branch (SBI, HDFC, ICICI etc.), fill Form-1 with the girl's birth certificate and guardian's KYC documents, and make the first deposit (Rs 250 to Rs 1.5 lakh) by cash, cheque or DD. A passbook is issued. Some banks (e.g. HDFC, Axis, IPPB) allow online opening for existing customers; subsequent deposits can usually be made via net banking or the India Post app.
source_document: National Savings Institute - Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme Rules (2014/2016/2019); Ministry of Finance quarterly interest rate notifications
